title: Adentris vs CodaMetrix: Coding vs Behavioral Health Compliance Compared
summary: Adentris vs CodaMetrix for behavioral health and SUD: autonomous coding at scale versus behavioral-health-specific documentation compliance with ASAM, 42 CFR Part 2, and denials.
body_markdown:
**The short version:** Adentris and CodaMetrix both aim to get the claim right, but they do different jobs in different settings. CodaMetrix is an autonomous coding platform that translates clinical notes into billing codes across radiology, pathology, surgery, and E/M for health systems. Adentris is a revenue integrity and documentation compliance layer purpose-built for behavioral health and SUD that checks whether the documentation supports the claim, with rules like ASAM level of care and 42 CFR Part 2 and an appeals and denials module, running on any EHR. If your problem is coding at scale, CodaMetrix is built for that. If your problem is behavioral health denials, that is where Adentris focuses.


Both aim to get the claim right, so the comparison comes down to whether the job is coding or behavioral-health documentation compliance. Here is an honest comparison.


## What Adentris does


Adentris is an AI platform for revenue integrity and documentation compliance built specifically for behavioral health and SUD programs. It works on top of the EHR you already run, connecting through an API or HL7 where one exists (for example Alleva, Pimsy, Kipu, Epic, or Athenahealth) and through a secure web agent where it does not, so there is no migration. It reviews notes in real time and flags the elements that get behavioral health claims denied before the claim is submitted: medical necessity, ASAM level-of-care justification, treatment plan updates, group therapy attendance, service units, signature timing, and 42 CFR Part 2 consent. When something is missing, it drafts the correction for the clinician to accept, and it pairs documentation review with an appeals and denials module. Adentris is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 certified, with 42 CFR Part 2 controls and BAAs in place.


## What CodaMetrix does


CodaMetrix is an autonomous medical coding platform, spun out of Mass General Brigham, whose CMX system translates clinical documentation into billing codes across specialties such as radiology, pathology, surgery, and evaluation and management. It has ranked at the top of autonomous coding in industry surveys and is used across many hospitals. For health systems that want to automate coding at scale, CodaMetrix is a strong, well-regarded option.

## Which should you choose?


Coding and documentation compliance are related but different. CodaMetrix assigns the codes automatically once the note exists, at scale across specialties. Adentris checks whether the documentation itself supports the claim for behavioral health and SUD, flagging a missing medical necessity statement, an unjustified ASAM level of care, or a missing 42 CFR Part 2 consent, drafting the fix before submission, and pairing review with an appeals and denials module. For a SUD program, that specialty depth and the pre-submission, documentation-level review are the practical differences, and the two could work together.


- **Choose CodaMetrix if** you are a health system that wants to automate medical coding at scale across radiology, pathology, surgery, and E/M.
- **Choose Adentris if** you run a behavioral health or SUD program and want the documentation itself checked against the specialty rules that drive denials, ASAM, medical necessity, and 42 CFR Part 2, with drafted fixes and appeals, on any EHR.


## Adentris as a CodaMetrix alternative for behavioral health documentation


If you are evaluating CodaMetrix for a behavioral health or SUD program, the question is what job you need done. Autonomous coding assigns the codes; it does not, by itself, confirm that the documentation supports a behavioral health claim. Adentris does that: it reviews the note against the rules that drive behavioral health and SUD denials, ASAM level of care, medical necessity, and 42 CFR Part 2, drafts the correction before submission, and pairs it with an appeals and denials workflow, running on any EHR through an API, HL7, or a secure web agent. It can complement autonomous coding or stand in where documentation compliance is the gap.


## How Adentris helps


For behavioral health and SUD organizations, the biggest revenue leak is documentation, and it is specific: medical necessity that was never shown, missing ASAM justification, a Part 2 consent that was not captured. Adentris reviews every chart in real time inside your existing EHR and flags exactly those gaps before the claim is filed, then drafts the fix, and it pairs that with an appeals and denials module so compliance and revenue integrity live in one place. In practice that means fewer denied claims, less audit exposure, and far less time spent reworking documentation after a payer pushes back. Adentris is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 certified, with 42 CFR Part 2 controls and BAAs in place. CodaMetrix automates the coding at scale; Adentris makes sure the behavioral health documentation supports the claim. For a SUD program, Adentris brings ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 depth, drafts the fix before submission, and pairs it with appeals, on any EHR.

## Frequently asked questions


**What is the difference between Adentris and CodaMetrix?**


CodaMetrix is an autonomous coding platform whose CMX system translates clinical notes into billing codes across specialties. Adentris is a revenue integrity and documentation compliance layer purpose-built for behavioral health and SUD that checks whether the documentation supports the claim, with ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 rules and an appeals module. CodaMetrix codes the note; Adentris makes sure the behavioral health documentation gets paid.


**Can Adentris and CodaMetrix be used together?**


Yes. They solve different halves of the problem, so a program can use CodaMetrix to code the notes automatically and Adentris to verify the documentation supports the claim and to handle appeals. Adentris reviews the note however it was written, so it fits alongside CodaMetrix.


**Is Adentris a good alternative to CodaMetrix?**


For programs whose problem is denials and audit exposure rather than autonomous coding at scale, yes. Adentris focuses on catching and correcting the behavioral health and SUD gaps that drive denials before submission, with ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 built in and an appeals and denials module, and it runs on any EHR without a migration.


**Which is better for a substance use disorder program?**


For SUD, the claims that get denied usually turn on ASAM level of care, medical necessity, and 42 CFR Part 2, which Adentris is built around with real-time, pre-submission review and drafted corrections. CodaMetrix is strong for autonomous coding across radiology, pathology, surgery, and E/M. Programs that want SUD-specific compliance depth and denials support often lean Adentris.
